reason: The kitchen ceiling leak is confirmed at a compression joint above the hatch (event-009, event-011). It recurred on 13 June when the tap was used (event-020). The authorised repair cannot go ahead. On the return visit the contractor found an unidentified pale fibrous lining and paused (event-017). We told him not to disturb it (event-018), and he left without opening the ceiling (event-023). No survey exists (event-006, event-013, event-022). A young child lives in the flat (event-007). The leak is ongoing and a possible hazardous material blocks the fix, so a person should decide how to proceed. I rate it P1, not P0: the tenant reports no electrics affected, no sagging, and only a small drip with the tap now out of use (event-003, event-020). The landlord's approval covers only the quoted plumbing scope (event-013). She has declined to extend it without cost and timing (event-022), and the contractor cannot price an assessment (event-023). I cannot approve spend or instruct more work, and routing for approval has no amount to cite. Waiting would leave a recurring leak with no route to repair. I already asked the landlord for a decision (event-024), and her reply is not overdue. If she authorises assessment, or the leak worsens, the plan changes. Escalating to the property manager gives a person the task of arranging the assessment and tenant advice.
unknowns: Identity of the lining and whether it contains asbestos
Cost and timing of an assessment
Whether the leak can be isolated
Landlord's decision on further scope
Amount of the approved estimate
options: Seek landlord authorisation for a specialist material assessment, with a quote, before any opening
Ask the contractor whether the supply can be isolated, and give the tenant safety advice including keeping the tap out of use
Treat as P0 and send on-call if the leak worsens, spreads, reaches electrics or the ceiling sags

actions.summary: Kitchen ceiling leak at 16 Brindlewick Mews is confirmed (leaking compression joint above the hatch) and recurs when the kitchen tap is used. The authorised repair is blocked. The contractor found an unidentified pale fibrous lining behind the ceiling board and stopped. A young child lives in the flat. A person needs to decide how to handle the suspect material and the ongoing leak. The landlord has only approved the quoted plumbing scope.
known: Tenant reported damp patch and drips on 2025-06-10 (event-001). No electrics affected, no sagging (event-003, event-020).
Mossbarrow Pipe Services saw moisture at a compression joint above the hatch with the tap running. The hatch is too small to reach the joint (event-009, event-011).
Landlord authorised the quoted plumbing scope only, up to the estimate, and wants to be contacted before any scope or cost increase (event-013). The estimate amount is not stated in the case.

On the 13 June return visit Kellan saw a pale fibrous-looking lining. He has not touched it, cannot identify it, and paused (event-017). Mara told him not to drill, cut, sample or remove (event-018) and he left without opening the ceiling (event-023).
No survey or ceiling alteration records exist. The landlord and building manager have none (event-006, event-013, event-022).
Tenant reported a small drip when the tap was used on the morning of 13 June and has stopped using that tap. A young child is present (event-007, event-020).

Landlord said her authorisation does not cover specialist material assessment and asked for likely cost and timing first (event-022). Mara has asked for a decision on further scope; nothing extra is agreed (event-024).
The communal roof inspection is planned for the week after 10 June (event-006).

tried: Asked the building manager about leaks and records (event-005, event-006)
Inspection, then quote, then landlord approval, then return visit (event-008 to event-016)
Stopped work and told the tenant not to touch the hatch or ceiling (event-018, event-019)
Sent the landlord an update requesting a decision on further scope (event-024). Her reply is not yet due.
options: Recommended: Ask the landlord to authorise a specialist asbestos/material assessment (get a quote first, as she asked) before any opening. Meanwhile ask the contractor whether the supply can be isolated or the tap/joint made safe without disturbing the lining.

Have the tenant keep the kitchen tap out of use and report any new drips or sagging. Send safety advice to the tenant (keep the child away from the area, do not disturb the ceiling) and set a short follow-up for the landlord's decision.
If the leak worsens, spreads, reaches electrics or the ceiling sags, treat it as P0 and send on-call. Consider a different contractor or a specialist if the landlord approves.
